To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) IL-7 stimulates osteoblasts to produce IL-7, 2) IL-7 upregulates the production of RANKL and macrophage-colony stimulating factor (M-CS) by T-cells, 3) RANKL and/or M-CS are essential for IL-7-mediated osteoclast formation, 4) osteoclast formation induced by IL-7 is not blocked by osteoproteger, and 5) IL-7
IL-7 is an osteoclastogenic factor that is induced by proinflammatory cytokines and acts via both RACK-dependent and RACK-independent mechanisms to stimulate osteoclast formation.
Interleukin-1 and TNFa stimulate stromal cell production IL-7, which in turn stimulates T cells to produce soluble RANKL and other cytokines that lead to increased osteoclast formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the formation of the bone-resorbing osteoclasts.
understanding the molecular mechanisms responsible for osteoclastogenesis and the regulation of bone resorption.

understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms responsible for the regulation of osteoclast differentiation and activation, and the development of novel therapeutics for osteoclast-associated diseases, such as osteoporosis, periodontitis, and rheumatoid arthritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-7 stimulates osteoblasts to produce RANKL and IL-7 stimulates T-cells to produce M-CSF.
IL-7 is a potent stimulator of osteoclast formation and bone resorption.
IL-7 is an important mediator of inflammatory bone loss and is a key regulator of osteoclast formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-7 is a key regulator of bone resorption.
IL-7 is an important mediator of bone resorption.
IL-7 is a novel osteoclastogenic factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-7 is an inflammatory cytokine that is produced by bone marrow stromal cells in response to IL-1 and tumor necrosis alpha (TNF-alpha).

IL-7 is an important cytokine that can stimulate osteoclast formation in a RANKL- and M-CSF-dependent manner and that IL-1 and tumor necrosis alpha (TNF-alpha) can stimulate osteoclastic bone resorption by inducing the production of IL-1 and IL-7 from the stromal cell.
IL-7 is not just an important factor in the development of the immune system but is also an important factor in bone homeostasis and that it is an important factor in inflammatory bone loss.
